done_when: Every review prompt carries the standards page (src/forge/standards.md), the same text the worker brief carries, as rules the reviewer checks the change against, and the review reports a change that breaks one of its rules as a finding that names the rule. A test runs a review through Forge's command and shows the page's text reaches the reviewer.

dismissals.because: src/forge/review.py:375 Autoreview is the third-party edge: Forge passes the page with Autoreview's own --prompt-file option (autoreview:7060, 'Additional review instruction file'), and the tests check exactly what crosses that edge. Whether a model then names a rule can't be proven by a deterministic test.

findings.body: The new tests inspect the text that the Autoreview stub reads from `--prompt-file`; they do not show that the reviewer receives it. The stub logs the file before launching Codex (`tests/stubs/autoreview:23-29`), while the Codex stub records only its folder and commit (`tests/test_close.py:24-31`). A helper that drops the prompt file would still pass these tests. The tests also supply a fixed clean report, so they never show a standards-breaking change producing a finding that names the rule. The required command-level test needs to observe the reviewer’s prompt and its finding for a violating change.
